title: Thursday, foam core
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday. The shop. Foam core. The owner doesn't ask about Monday or Tuesday; she wasn't in the strip for them. She asks about the diploma from Wednesday. Wood cuts. The strip has never mentioned Seattle and doesn't now.

panels.composition: The shop's backroom. WOOD cutting foam core. The OWNER in the door with a job ticket.

image.prompt: a young man cutting foam core in a frame shop backroom while a woman in reading glasses stands in the doorway holding a job ticket, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The diploma, framed, on the counter. Cream and green.

image.prompt: close on a framed diploma in a cream and green double mat on a shop counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner looking at Wood a beat longer than the ticket needs.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses looking at a young man a moment longer than necessary, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner going. Wood cutting. The blade, clean. Nothing about Monday. Nothing about Tuesday. The strip has a week it doesn't mention and this is the first day of not mentioning it.

image.prompt: a young man cutting foam core cleanly in a quiet backroom, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Nothing about Monday or Tuesday. The first day of not mentioning it. (dw_2000-09-20: 'They held up.')
